A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CROP and are readable throughout, including equations, tables, figures and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched reliably. V1's final visualization appendix contains only a heading; v2 supplies substantive additional material.

before.justification: V1 reports original CROP evaluations on LLaVA-1.5-7B/13B, region-only pruning experiments and an anchor-token ablation in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds evaluations on other backbones, inference timings, pruning-layer ablations, annotated localization measurements and qualitative success/failure cases.

M1.justification: The Qwen2-VL-2B localizer, 8×8 region representation, region-guided ILP and PLC query/anchor fusion remain unchanged, including Equations (1)–(5). Additional backbone evaluations and implementation explanations do not introduce a new pruning rule or compression component.

E1.justification: The training sources and six VQA benchmarks are retained, as are the question-guided localization and VQA tasks. The new annotated TextVQA study and qualitative cases examine existing coverage; additional backbones change model configurations. ScienceQA remains image-only despite its shortened table label.

E2.justification: V2 removes MustDrop at all three budgets and FasterVLM at 64 tokens from the 7B comparison in v1 Table 2. Conversely, v2 Table 2 adds SparseVLM and PDrop to the 13B comparisons previously reported in v1 Table 3. These materially revise comparator participation.

E3.justification: V2 adds NeXT multi-crop and Qwen variable-token configurations, 13B PLC, timing measurements, a pruning-layer sweep and a 3,000-sample localization protocol with area recall and size-matched controls. The 13B aggregate now includes POPE. Section 4.1 also explicitly includes instruction-following data in localizer training, revising the reported setting without establishing that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original region-only and anchor-removal studies survive as v2 Tables 5–6. Appendices D–E add pruning-layer sensitivity, localization accuracy against manual annotations, ground-truth/center/random region controls, and success/failure cases examining relational and global-context questions.

E5.justification: Appendix C in both versions says results are averaged across multiple experimental runs. Neither supplies run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new sample counts and recall summaries do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial backbone, timing, pruning-layer and localization results, including mean localization recall of 0.9477 in Table 9. Retained 7B benchmark scores are unchanged. The 13B 64-token aggregate changes from 95.7% to 96.2% after adding POPE; scores on the original five benchmarks remain unchanged, so this is not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The coordinate constraints and mathematical constructions in Equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. V2's standard area-recall description supports empirical evaluation rather than introducing new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution list retain the same central claims: contextual-region-guided pruning, a reusable localizer, PLC and ILP strategies, and strong performance without retraining the main VLM for ILP. The additional experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of overlapping localization with backbone execution, pruning-depth tradeoffs and dependence on localization quality. Appendix E identifies failures when a single region omits relational or global information and proposes multiple regions as future work. These substantially extend v1's discussion, whose explicit limitation concerned training overhead.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the future code/data-release promise with a stated release and repository address, clarifies ground-truth-box use and VisionZip's fine-tuned variant, and removes boundary markers from Appendix A's response template. Most training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Section 4.1 changes localizer training time from 8 to 12 hours, although Section 3.2 still says 8.

R1.justification: Related work expands from two subsections to four, adding general LLM literature and chain-of-thought/locate-then-answer approaches such as V*, TextCoT, Argus and MRFD. V2 explicitly positions coarse block localization against precise bounding-box prediction and model-specific fine-tuning, substantially broadening its research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 standardizes much of the terminology from key or continuous regions to contextual regions, edits the introduction, shortens the conclusion, and restructures related work. Additional experiments receive new subsections and appendices, while the core method and original analysis largely retain their wording and organization.

P2.justification: V2 merges the separate 7B/13B tables into a wide side-by-side Table 2, adds six experimental tables and three case-study figures, and revises schematic highlights and grid labels. Existing ablations are relocated and renumbered. Figure 2's caption also acquires stray citation-key text.

improvement.justification: V1 supports efficiency mainly through token reduction and validates localization largely through downstream results. V2 adds measured inference times, independent-backbone evaluations, annotated localization controls and explicit failure analyses, substantially strengthening empirical support and applicability assessment. Dropped comparators and reporting defects—including conflicting training times and incorrect NeXT token-count headings—reduce polish and precision, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
